text:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN PROPOSED FIX - please read before implementing.

I recommended hashing the sparse triplet @i, @p, @x, @Dim. I validated that recommendation and it is INCOMPLETE. Implemented naively it would introduce a provenance correctness bug: two mathematically identical frames can receive different signatures.

The failure case is a stored explicit zero. dgCMatrix keeps a sparsity PATTERN, and a stored entry whose value is 0 is retained in @x unless dropped. Two matrices that are equal as matrices can therefore have different @i/@p/@x.

Measured. A0 has one stored zero (199 stored entries); B0 = drop0(A0) has 198. They are equal as dense matrices:

  identical(as.matrix(A0), as.matrix(B0))  TRUE      <- ground truth: same matrix
  dense signature equal                    TRUE      <- current behaviour, correct
  naive sparse-triplet signature equal     FALSE     <- my original suggestion, WRONG
  canonicalized sparse signature equal     TRUE      <- correct

CORRECTED FIX - canonicalize before hashing:

  weights <- Matrix::drop0(
    as(as(frame$weights, "CsparseMatrix"), "generalMatrix")
  )
  semantic <- list(
    representation = frame$representation,
    weights = list(i = weights@i, p = weights@p, x = weights@x, dim = weights@Dim),
    normalization = frame$normalization,
    domain = frame$domain,
    index = frame$index,
    specification = frame$specification
  )

drop0 removes stored zeros, and forcing CsparseMatrix + generalMatrix pins one representation so a symmetric or triangular subclass cannot hash differently from an equal general matrix.

Sanity retained after canonicalization: a single entry perturbed by 1e-12 still produces a DIFFERENT signature, so the fix does not blunt sensitivity.

Verified unchanged from my earlier note: the round-trip T->C sparse conversion, a double transpose, and an assignment that changes nothing all keep the signature stable, and genuinely different matrices (new nonzero, different dims) all separate correctly.

Whether a stored zero is reachable in practice through the current .normalize_frame paths I did not establish. It does not matter much - hashing a representation-dependent structure is fragile regardless, since a different construction route or a future Matrix version could introduce one. Canonicalizing costs one drop0 call and removes the whole class of problem.

The p0 memory finding itself is unchanged: 18.6 GiB dense coercion at p=50000, and the canonicalized sparse hash is still ~1657x smaller.
